title: Products Nobody Bought
description: List the products that appear in no order item.
statement: Return the `name` and `category` of every product that has **never been ordered**: no row of `order_items` refers to it. Alphabetical by `name`.
variants: INSERT INTO products VALUES (110, 'Ghost Product', 'toys', 5.0), (111, 'Another Ghost', 'books', 7.0)
hints: Keep every product, and look for matching rows in `order_items`.
After a `LEFT JOIN`, a product with no matching item has `NULL` in all the columns of `order_items`.
Test a column of `order_items` for `IS NULL`, not a column of `products`.
solution:
SELECT p.name, p.category
FROM products AS p
LEFT JOIN order_items AS i ON i.product_id = p.id
WHERE i.product_id IS NULL
ORDER BY p.name;
explanation:
**The idea.** The same anti-join as for customers with no orders, written the other way: `LEFT JOIN` keeps every product, and `WHERE i.product_id IS NULL` keeps only the products for which no item was found.

**Two forms, one meaning.** `NOT EXISTS` and `LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL` give the same rows; which one is faster depends on the database and its optimiser, and the right choice is the one you can read. Test the `IS NULL` on a column of the *right* table that can never be `NULL` for a real match (a key or `NOT NULL` column).

**Usual mistakes.** Testing a column of the left table for `NULL`; an inner join (it returns the products that *were* ordered).
